findings.title: Wrong lightness pair for embedded post author links
findings.body: The embedded-post author link color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Both arguments are wrong for preserving the original appearance: the light-theme value should stay at 30%, and the dark-theme value should use the complementary 70% of `$secondary` (as done for the equivalent quote-title styling). As written, the light theme gets a much lighter, low-contrast link and the dark theme gets the opposite end of the scale.

findings.title: Custom message length color lightness is reversed
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The lightness pair is reversed: the light-theme argument changed from 70% to 30%, and the dark-theme argument from the expected 30% to 70%. The equivalent rule in `desktop/modal.scss` uses `primary 70% / secondary 30%`. This makes the mobile custom-message-length text darker in the light theme and lighter in the dark theme than intended.

findings.title: Topic map heading lost its intended 20% lightness
findings.body: The `.topic-map h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Unlike the desktop topic-map rule, which correctly uses `primary 20% / secondary 80%`, this changes the light-theme color from 20% to 50% and does not derive the dark-theme value correctly. The section heading becomes noticeably lighter and loses the intended emphasis.

findings.title: Group member name color no longer preserves 30% lightness
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% and not using the complementary 70% for the dark theme. This makes the member name lighter and removes the intentional emphasis relative to the adjacent title.

findings.title: Mobile group member name uses the wrong lightness pair
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses the 50%/50% pair instead of preserving 30% for the light theme and using 70% of `$secondary` for the dark theme. The same mistake exists in the desktop user stylesheet, and it makes the name less emphasized than before.

findings.title: Category badge notification color missed the dark-theme conversion
findings.body: The `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` color is still `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while every other similar color in this file was wrapped with `dark-light-choose`. In a dark theme `$primary` is the light foreground color, so this produces a very light count color instead of a muted value derived from the dark `$secondary`. This leaves the badge inconsistent with the rest of the dark-theme conversion and can make it stand out too strongly.
